newsitem.title: EGYPT: Greek deputy urges EU role in Mideast peace process.
newsitem.headline: Greek deputy urges EU role in Mideast peace process.

text.p: Greece's deputy foreign minister said on Tuesday he would convey Egypt's position on the Middle East peace process to the European Union to help formulate the bloc's policy on efforts to restart peace talks.

Yannos Kranidiotis also said he relayed Egypt's position to his counterparts in the United Nations, where Egypt has sought a special session to discuss Israeli practises which it sees as hindering peace with the Palestinians.

"We have every concern and interest to assist and help the continuation of the peace process and to convey to the parties concerned our deep conviction that the agreements as have been agreed should be implemented," Kranidiotis told reporters.
He spoke after meeting Egypt's Foreign Minister Amr Moussa as part of a tour including Syria, Lebanon and Jordan to follow up a visit to Israel and Gaza by Greece's foreign minister.

"We would like to take necessary steps for a more active European Union involvement in the peace process," he said. "The message and information I give to our European Union partners will certainly help the formulation of the EU position in the future," said Kranidiotis.
The United States, main sponsor of previous peace efforts by Israelis and Palestinians, has so far not succeeded in bringing the two sides together to the negotiating table.
Kranidiotis said there was no specific Greek initiative but it was operating in the context of the EU, which has designated a special peace envoy to the region, Miguel Moratinos.
Talks between Palestinians and Israelis have stalled since March when Israel broke ground for a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Egypt has an active role in Middle East peace brokering.
It has asked the U.N. for a special session to discuss Israeli practises such as building Jewish settlements, which have sparked unrest with the Palestinians.

"What I have promised my Egyptian counterparts is that I would transmit his point of view to the European partners and encourage them to support it. But you know that with Greece forming part of the EU it would firstly prefer to have a consensus among the EU so Europeans can vote as a united group," Kranidiotis.
Kranidiotis also said Greece believed agreement between Israel and Turkey to hold military exercises "changes the balance in the area and undermines peace and stability."
